A 36-year-old female presents to the emergency department with acute onset of severe head and neck
pain that developed over 8 hours. Her vital signs show a temperature of 39.0°C, heart rate of 125 beats
per minute, and blood pressure of 117/84 mm Hg. While in the emergency department, she
experiences a brief 10-second generalized tonic-clonic seizure that resolves spontaneously. Her
Covid-19 vaccinations are current, and SARS-CoV-2 testing is negative. Laboratory findings show: | |
Patient value | Reference range | | --- | --- | --- | | Leukocyte count (per mm3) | 15,000 | 4500–11,000 | |
Hemoglobin (g/dL) | 13.1 | 12.0–16.0 | | Glucose (mg/dL) | 100 | 70–100 | | Sodium (mEq/liter) | 138 |
136–145 | Following blood culture collection and initiation of dexamethasone and empiric antimicrobial
therapy, what is the most appropriate next step in this patient's evaluation? Answer Choices: (A) Order
MRI of the brain (B) Perform lumbar puncture (C) Initiate antiepileptic therapy before imaging (D)
Perform EEG to evaluate seizure activity (E) Perform CT of the head (F) Initiate antiviral therapy before
imaging (G) Perform MRI of the brain (H) Measure serum ammonia levels (I) Obtain a chest X-ray to
rule out infection (J) Repeat blood cultures before further imaging
 A. Measure serum ammonia levels
B. Order MRI of the brain
C. Obtain a chest X-ray to rule out infection
D. Repeat blood cultures before further imaging
E. Perform MRI of the brain
F. Perform lumbar puncture
G. Perform CT of the head
H. Perform EEG to evaluate seizure activity
I. Initiate antiviral therapy before imaging
J. Initiate antiepileptic therapy before imaging
